battle.name: 皮亞瑪-拉杜起義
battle.theater: 安納托利亞西部阿爾茲瓦、威盧薩
battle.brief: 公元前1260至前1255年，皮亞瑪-拉杜在西安納托利亞起兵，聯同阿希亞瓦與米利都宗主阿特帕，襲擾阿爾茲瓦、塞哈河地與威盧薩等赫梯附庸。附庸馬納帕-塔爾洪塔驅逐失敗，赫梯王哈圖西里三世親征，聯軍潰散。埃及月牙劍並未出現在安納托利亞，它代表同一時代埃及與赫梯共同面對西方的軍力。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 交戰雙方是前13世紀的安納托利亞強權赫梯王國，與皮亞瑪-拉杜率領的西部安納托利亞叛軍聯盟。赫梯以哈圖沙為都，王權集中於「大王」一身；軍隊以王室直屬的步兵與弓箭手為主，前代已棄雙人戰車，作戰全靠徒步結陣。拉杜一方並非單一部族的農兵，他以「大王」自居，出身很可能與被赫梯廢黜的阿爾茲瓦舊王室相關，靠聯姻把西安納托利亞西岸的城邦網絡拉到自己一方：他把女兒嫁給米利都的附庸宗主阿特帕；同時與阿希亞瓦，即邁錫尼希臘人在西安納托利亞建立的政權，結為對付赫梯的攻擊同盟。聯軍的另一端是赫梯在北部與西部的附庸與鄰邦，如伊蘇瓦、塞哈河地一帶的小邦，站在赫梯一邊。拉杜的起事不是一次襲擊，而是橫掃阿爾茲瓦、塞哈河地、萊斯博斯島與威盧薩一帶附庸城邑的長期戰事，前後威脅三位赫梯大王。關於他的勢力核心究竟在北安納托利亞的卡斯卡山區，還是在阿爾茲瓦故地與特洛伊周邊，學界至今分歧，這正是本場戰爭記載有限最好的證明。埃及不在交戰名單上，卻是赫梯在同一時期的外交夥伴，兩國在前14世紀的阿瑪爾納書簡中曾就西方問題互通消息。
countriesEn: The two sides are the Hittite kingdom, the Anatolian power of the thirteenth century BCE with its capital at Hattusa and its authority concentrated in the person of the Great King, and a rebel coalition in western Anatolia led by Piyamaradu. The Hittite army was built around the king's own infantry and archers; chariot warfare had already been abandoned by their predecessors, so the army fought entirely on foot in close order. Piyamaradu's side was not a levy of one tribal peasants. He called himself a Great King, and his descent was probably tied to the old royal house of Arzawa that the Hittites had deposed; he drew the city-state network of the western Anatolian coast into his own camp by marriage, giving his daughter to Atpa, the vassal ruler of Millawanda (Miletus), while at the same time forming an offensive alliance against Hatti with Ahhiyawa, the Mycenaean Greek power established in western Anatolia. On the other side of the line stood the Hittite vassals and neighbours of the north and west, such as Isuwa and the small principalities of the Seha River Land, who took the Hittite side. Piyamaradu's rising was not a single raid but a long series of campaigns against the dependent cities of Arzawa, the Seha River Land, Lazpa on Lesbos and Wilusa, and it menaced three successive Hittite Great Kings. Whether the core of his power lay in the Kaska highlands of northern Anatolia or in the old Arzawa country around Troy is still disputed by scholars, which is the clearest proof that the record of this war is thin. Egypt is not on the list of belligerents, but it was a diplomatic partner of Hatti in the same period, and the two states exchanged news about western problems in the Amarna letters of the fourteenth century BCE.
people: 皮亞瑪-拉杜是這場戰爭唯一的中心人物。他的名字是盧語詞 piyama（贈禮）與 aradu（信士）的複合，赫梯書吏在書簡裡罵他是「滋事者」「冒險家」「流寇」乃至「傭兵」，說明他在敵方檔案中的形象幾乎是亂源本身。學者認為他很可能是被穆瓦塔里二世廢黜的阿爾茲瓦王烏哈-齊提的後人，甚至可能是其子皮亞馬-庫倫塔之子，但從未在文本中以王子身份出現，故布賴斯等人只稱他為「叛亂的赫梯顯貴」。他的關鍵動作是向赫梯大王請求被接納為附庸王、恢復舊國的繼承權，遭拒後立即反叛，轉而向阿希亞瓦的大王求助，並靠聯姻拉攏米利都。哈圖西里三世是鎮壓他的赫梯大王，其妻普杜赫帕是首席女祭司，她的祈禱文獻記載自己曾到海邊獻祭，求海神出手把拉杜捉拿歸案。赫梯先後派遣的附庸馬納帕-塔爾洪塔受命驅逐拉杜卻告失敗，才改派王軍出征。塔瓦加拉瓦與阿特帕則代表米利都方面，書簡中對大王控訴拉杜的騷擾。拉杜的前後任對手穆瓦塔里二世、哈圖西里三世與圖德哈利亞，至少要在名冊上被記上一筆。
peopleEn: Piyamaradu is the single central figure of this war. His name is a compound of the Luwian words piyama, gift, and aradu, devotee, and the Hittite scribes in their letters call him a troublemaker, an adventurer, a freebooter and even a mercenary, which tells us how completely he dominates the enemy record. Scholars believe he was probably a descendant of Uhha-Ziti, the king of Arzawa deposed by Muwatalli II, and possibly the son of that king's son Piyama-Kurunta, but he is never referred to as a prince in any text, so Bryce and others prefer to call him a rebellious Hittite dignitary. His decisive move was to ask the Great King of Hatti to accept him as a vassal king and to restore his hereditary claim; when he was refused he rebelled at once, turned to the Great King of Ahhiyawa for support, and consolidated the western coast through marriage, giving his daughter to Atpa of Millawanda. Hattusili III was the Hittite king who crushed him; his consort Puduhepa, chief priestess, left a votive prayer recording that she travelled to the sea to make an offering so that the god of the sea would apprehend Piyamaradu. The vassal Manapa-Tarhunta, whom the Hittites first ordered to drive Piyamaradu out, failed and was replaced by the royal army. Tawagalawa and Atpa speak for Miletus in the correspondence, complaining to the Great King about Piyamaradu's harassment. His Hittite adversaries in turn, Muwatalli II, Hattusili III and Tudhaliya, all have to be entered in the ledger of the men who had to deal with him.
kits: 本場戰爭的直接文獻裡沒有出現埃及月牙劍，這點必須先講清楚。赫梯與邁錫尼的戰爭記錄從未點名這種彎刃單刃劍，赫梯的近戰主力是銅斧。但月牙劍本身的來歷，正好落在這場衝突的地理與年代上：它源自新月形戰斧，前16世紀傳入埃及，前1500年前後已定型，至前13世紀中葉大致退出一線序列，只餘儀仗、頒賜與象徵之用；同一型式的鐮刀形劍在前18世紀的黎凡特出土物（例如納布魯斯一件飾以金銀合金鑲片的月牙劍）仍可見到，說明這門技術正沿著金屬與工藝的通道往西傳。實際在安納托利亞交手的武器另有三套：赫梯步兵持銅斧、長矛、短劍，配小型皮盾，使用弓與投石索；阿希亞瓦方面用邁錫尼式青銅長劍、青銅頭盔與銅胸甲，另有雙人戰車與投石索；拉杜的民兵用投槍、小圓盾與斧，另有大量木器。馬匹是不鞍不鎧的輕型馬，車輛只有雙輪與四輪兩種，用於運載掠物。攻城器械在文獻中無一記載，這場戰爭靠的是燒城、破壞與劫走牲畜。
kitsEn: No Egyptian khopesh appears in the direct documents of this war, and that has to be stated first. The Hittite and Mycenaean accounts never name a curved single-edged sword of that type, and the Hittite close-combat arm was the copper axe. The pedigree of the khopesh, however, falls exactly across the geography and the date of this conflict: it developed from the crescent-shaped battle axe, reached Egypt in the sixteenth century BCE, was standardised by about 1500 BCE, and by the middle of the thirteenth century had largely left the line of battle, surviving as ceremonial issue, royal gift and symbol. Sickle-shaped swords of the same family still occur in Levantine finds, such as the khopesh with electrum inlay from Nablus dated to the eighteenth century BCE, which shows the craft travelling west along the same channels that carried metal and technique. Three other sets of weapons were actually used in Anatolia: Hittite infantry carried copper axes, spears and short swords with small hide shields, together with bows and slings; the Ahhiyawa side used Mycenaean-style bronze swords, bronze helmets and bronze body armour, plus two-horse chariots and slings; Piyamaradu's levies used javelins, small round shields and axes, with a good deal of wooden equipment. The horses were light, unsaddled and unarmoured, and the only vehicles were two-wheeled and four-wheeled carts used to haul loot. There is not a single siege engine in the record, because this war was fought by burning towns, breaking roads and driving off cattle.
tactics: 聯軍的戰法是游擊而非會戰。拉杜不去攻守備森嚴的王都，而是逐一襲擊赫梯的附庸城邑：燒掉聚落、拆毀莊園、趕走牲畜，再帶著戰利品退回山區或退回海邊的島嶼。赫梯方面的戰術是步兵縱隊沿河谷推進，弓箭手在前、斧兵在後，關鍵是封死南北向的塞哈河走廊，把西岸的城邦一個個切開；大王常親自領兵，並靠戰利品與徵發維持遠征的糧秣。赫梯第一次派附庸馬納帕-塔爾洪塔去驅逐拉杜就失敗，說明雜牌附庸軍無法在山區與拉杜周旋，必須由王室直屬的步兵接手。拉杜的聯軍還有一層外交戰：他把女兒嫁給米利都宗主阿特帕，等於在敵方腹地安插自己的血親；赫梯的對策是大量寫書簡，向各附庸發動公文圍堵，並在祈禱文獻裡把捉拿拉杜說成神意。阿希亞瓦的船隊從海上來，劫掠之後照例不歸，赫梯因此把他們視為海盜而非可信的盟友。季節也左右戰局：安納托利亞西部山多雨雪，遠征多在夏秋發動，渡口與河口是瓶頸。
tacticsEn: The coalition fought by raiding rather than by set-piece battle. Piyamaradu did not lay siege to a well-defended royal city; he hit the Hittite dependencies one at a time, burning settlements, breaking up estates, driving off the cattle and then withdrawing with the loot back into the hills or out to the islands. The Hittite method was an infantry column pushing along the river valleys, archers in front and axe-men behind, the decisive business being to close the north-south corridor of the Seha river and to cut the western city-states apart; the Great King often led in person, and the campaign was supplied by plunder and requisition. The Hittite first attempt, sending the vassal Manapa-Tarhunta to drive Piyamaradu out, failed, which showed that mixed vassal levies could not manoeuvre against him in the mountains and that the king's own infantry had to take over. Piyamaradu also fought a diplomatic war: by marrying his daughter to Atpa of Miletus he planted his own blood inside the enemy heartland, and the Hittite answer was a flood of letters warning the dependencies, together with votive texts presenting the capture of Piyamaradu as the work of the gods. The Ahhiyawa fleets came by sea and, true to form, sailed home again after the plunder, so the Hittites treated them as pirates rather than reliable allies. The season shaped the campaign as well: western Anatolia is mountainous and snowy in winter, expeditions were mounted in summer and autumn, and the crossings and river mouths were the chokepoints.
data: 可核對的數字不多，且多數來自現代斷代。戰爭的年代區間一般定在前1260至前1255年，此說出自布賴斯二〇〇五年《赫梯王國》一書，並為英文《戰爭列表：1000年前》所採用。拉杜的活動被認為至少延續三十五年，橫跨穆瓦塔里二世、哈圖西里三世與圖德哈利亞三朝；這條線索出自貝克曼、布賴斯與萊因二〇一一年《阿希雅瓦文本》的整理。三位赫梯王的在位年份可作對照：穆瓦塔里二世約前1295至前1272年，哈圖西里三世約前1267至前1240年，圖德哈利亞三世約前1240至前1205年。地理尺度可估：阿爾茲瓦的核心在蓋迪茲河谷，即今馬尼薩與厄菲斯一帶；塞哈河地就是今塞伊漢河流域；萊斯博斯島與安納托利亞大陸岸相隔約八公里；威盧薩即特洛伊平原，位於特洛伊東南方。兵器方面，月牙劍平均長五十至六十厘米，僅弧端外刃開鋒，通行服役期一般認為止於前1300年，約前1500年定型。兵力與傷亡一律無數可據：赫梯的書簡與頌歌只作修辭描述，不給編制與損失數字，前13世紀安納托利亞的兵役為徵召制，也無常備人口統計，本卡因此不列任何兵員與死傷估算。
dataEn: Few figures can be checked, and most of them come from modern dating rather than from the event itself. The war is generally placed between 1260 and 1255 BCE, a dating taken from Trevor Bryce's The Kingdom of the Hittites of 2005 and adopted by the English List of wars: before 1000. Piyamaradu's activity is held to have lasted at least thirty-five years, spanning the reigns of Muwatalli II, Hattusili III and Tudhaliya, a thread drawn from Beckman, Bryce and Cline's edition of the Ahhiyawa texts in 2011. The reigns of the three Hittite kings give a scale for comparison: Muwatalli II roughly 1295 to 1272 BCE, Hattusili III roughly 1267 to 1240 BCE, Tudhaliya III roughly 1240 to 1205 BCE. Geography can be estimated. The core of Arzawa lay in the Gediz valley, in the region of modern Manisa and Ephesus; the Seha River Land is the valley of the modern Seyhan river; the island of Lazpa lies about eight kilometres off the Anatolian mainland; and Wilusa is the Troad, southeast of Troy. As for the weapon itself, a khopesh averages fifty to sixty centimetres, is sharpened only along the outer part of the curve, and is generally held to have gone out of service around 1300 BCE after being standardised by about 1500 BCE. Troop strength and casualties are simply not available: the Hittite letters and songs describe the fighting in rhetoric and give no establishment and no loss figures, service in Anatolia was a levy system without standing population statistics, and this card therefore lists no estimate of numbers engaged or of losses.
cause: 起事的前因是赫梯在安納托利亞西部的宗主權擴張。穆瓦塔里二世攻滅阿爾茲瓦王國，廢黜其王烏哈-齊提，舊王室成員隨之流散；皮亞瑪-拉杜很可能出自這批失去國土的舊人，他手中握著一整套對西部城邦的傳統權利要求。當他向赫梯大王請求被接納為附庸王時，得到的不是承認而是拒絕，這道拒絕就是直接導火線。拉杜隨即轉向阿希亞瓦求援：邁錫尼方面的西岸政權要的正是安納托利亞腹地的金屬、奴隸與港口，與赫梯爭的是同一批城邑，扶植拉杜可以牽制哈圖沙。第三重原因是赫梯的附庸體系本身出了裂縫，西部與北部的城邑在地理上彼此分散，一旦拉杜逐個攻擊阿爾茲瓦、塞哈河地、萊斯博斯與威盧薩的屬地，哈圖沙就無法同時防守。最後一點是前13世紀的安納托利亞沒有第三方大國可以仲裁這類邊界爭端，氏族與城邦只認自己的強人，於是失去國土者與覬覦內地者都匯到拉杜的旗號之下。
causeEn: The proximate cause of the rising was the spread of Hittite overlordship in western Anatolia. Muwatalli II destroyed the kingdom of Arzawa and deposed its king Uhha-Ziti, scattering the old royal house; Piyamaradu most probably came out of that group of dispossessed, and he carried with him a whole inherited claim on the western cities. When he asked the Great King of Hatti to accept him as a vassal king, what he received was not recognition but refusal, and that refusal is the immediate spark. He turned at once to Ahhiyawa for support: the Mycenaean power on the western coast wanted exactly what the Hittites wanted, the metal, the slaves and the harbours of the Anatolian interior, and the two were competing for the same cities, so backing Piyamaradu was a way of tying down Hattusa. A third cause lay in the fissures of the Hittite vassal system itself. The dependent towns of the west and north were widely separated, and once Piyamaradu struck Arzawa, the Seha River Land, Lazpa and Wilusa one after another, Hattusa could not defend them all at once. A final point is that in the thirteenth-century Anatolia there was no third great power able to arbitrate such a border dispute; clans and city-states recognised only their own strong men, and men without a country and men eyeing the interior both gathered under Piyamaradu's banner.
impact: 拉杜的失敗讓赫梯得以重新整頓西部的附庸體系，但他的名字也留在了書簡與祈禱文獻裡，成為赫梯書寫「叛亂者」時的原型範本，後來任何西部強人作亂，都可能被套上同一套修辭。更長遠的影響在愛琴海與安納托利亞的關係上：阿希亞瓦在赫梯眼中是以掠奪為業、來而不歸的海上一方，這個形象延續到前13世紀末，成為赫梯與拉美西斯二世在外交上彼此試探時的背景，也為其後卡疊什之戰前的格局埋下伏線。西部城邦的權力次序被重新排列，阿爾茲瓦故地與萊斯博斯回到赫梯附庸體系的控制，米利都一類海港則繼續是愛琴海勢力與安納托利亞腹地之間的交換點。兵器史上的意義同樣清楚：月牙劍在埃及退出一線裝備的同時，鐮刀形單刃劍的技術在黎凡特與安納托利亞的工坊裡延續，但安納托利亞戰場的近戰主力始終是斧，說明這場戰爭並沒有把埃及的象徵性兵器帶進山區。安納托利亞西部與黑海沿岸的青銅時代窖藏，則留下城邑被破壞之後金屬重新流動的痕跡。
impactEn: Piyamaradu's defeat allowed the Hittites to reorganise their western dependencies, but his name stayed in the letters and the votive prayers and became the archetype of the rebel in Hittite rhetoric; any later strong man rising in the west could be fitted into the same set of formulas. The more durable effect lies in the relationship between the Aegean and Anatolia. Ahhiyawa, in Hittite eyes, was a seafaring party that plundered and sailed home again, and that image persisted into the late thirteenth century, colouring the mutual probing between Hatti and Ramesses II and forming part of the background to the diplomatic landscape before the battle of Kadesh. The hierarchy of the western cities was rearranged, with old Arzawan territory and Lazpa brought back under the Hittite system of dependencies, while harbours such as Miletus remained the exchange point between the Aegean powers and the Anatolian interior. The significance for the history of arms is equally clear. At the moment the khopesh was leaving the first line in Egypt, the craft of the sickle-shaped single-edged sword was being carried on in the workshops of the Levant and Anatolia, yet the close-combat arm of the Anatolian battlefield remained the axe, which shows that this war did not carry the symbolic Egyptian weapon into the mountains. The Late Bronze Age hoards of western Anatolia and the Black Sea coast preserve, in turn, the traces of metal moving again after towns were broken.
result: 結果是聯軍潰散、拉杜從赫梯檔案中消失。米利都方面的書簡在提到他時已說他成了「過去的人」，這意味著至少有一次重大的失敗把他逐出了舞台；但哈圖西里三世王后普杜赫帕的祈禱文獻仍在祈求海神出手捉拿他，可見抓住本人在當時仍屬未竟之事。赫梯的處置方式很清楚：先派心腹附庸馬納帕-塔爾洪塔驅逐失敗，再由大王親率王軍遠征，摧毀城邑、焚燒山地聚落、掠回牲畜與俘虜，把西部與北部的附庸重新收編。聯盟隨之瓦解，阿特帕與拉杜女兒的婚約無法延續，阿希亞瓦的船隊照例在劫掠後退海。長期看來，拉杜一系在文獻中完全消失，西部安納托利亞的附庸體系在哈圖西里三世及其後任手中重建，赫梯由此騰出手來，把力量投向更南邊的敘利亞與埃及。另一層影響是文學的：前13世紀末威盧薩的城邦記憶進入希臘口傳，學界有人認為拉杜的經歷可能成為《伊利亞特》英雄傳說的底層素材，但這仍屬文學推測，不是史實定論。
resultEn: The outcome was the dispersal of the coalition and the disappearance of Piyamaradu from the Hittite archives. The correspondence from the Miletus side already refers to him as a figure of the past, which means that at least one heavy defeat drove him off the stage; but the votive prayer of Hattusili III's consort Puduhepa still asks the god of the sea to apprehend him, so that catching the man himself was evidently still an unfinished task. The Hittite manner of dealing with it is plain: first the trusted vassal Manapa-Tarhunta was sent to drive Piyamaradu out and failed, then the Great King led the royal army in person, destroyed cities, burned the mountain settlements, drove back the cattle and the captives, and took the western and northern dependencies back into hand. The alliance fell apart with it, the marriage between Atpa and Piyamaradu's daughter could not be carried on, and the Ahhiyawa fleets withdrew to sea after the plunder as always. In the long run the Piyamaradu line vanishes completely from the texts, the system of Hittite dependencies in western Anatolia is rebuilt under Hattusili III and his successors, and Hatti is thereby free to turn its strength south towards Syria and Egypt. A second layer of consequence is literary: the memory of the cities of Wilusa in the late thirteenth century entered Greek oral tradition, and some scholars hold that Piyamaradu's career may lie at the bottom of the heroic legend of the Iliad, though that remains literary inference rather than an established fact.
